title: Romans Chapter 15 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Romans chapter 15 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Romans Chapter 15 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Romans Chapter 15.

questions.question: In Romans 15, which of the following appears FIRST in the chapter?
options: We then that are strong ought to bear the infirmities of the weak
Let every one of us please his neighbour
For even Christ pleased not himself
Now the God of patience and consolation grant you
questions.correctAnswer: We then that are strong ought to bear the infirmities of the weak
questions.explanation: This is the first statement in Romans 15:1.

questions.question: What should every one of us do according to Romans 15:2?
options: Please his neighbour for his good
Bear the infirmities of the weak
questions.correctAnswer: Please his neighbour for his good
questions.explanation: Romans 15:2 states that we should please our neighbour for his good to edification.

questions.question: Who pleased not himself according to Romans 15:3?
questions.explanation: Romans 15:3 states that even Christ pleased not himself.

questions.question: According to Romans 15:4, why were things written aforetime?
questions.explanation: Romans 15:4 explains that things written aforetime were written for our learning.

questions.question: What does Romans 15:5 ask God to grant us?
questions.explanation: Romans 15:5 requests that God grant us to be likeminded one toward another.

questions.question: How are we to glorify God according to Romans 15:6?
options: With one mind and one mouth
questions.correctAnswer: With one mind and one mouth
questions.explanation: Romans 15:6 states that we may glorify God with one mind and one mouth.

questions.question: According to Romans 15:7, how should we receive one another?
questions.explanation: Romans 15:7 instructs us to receive one another as Christ also received us.

questions.question: What was Jesus Christ a minister of according to Romans 15:8?
questions.explanation: Romans 15:8 states that Jesus Christ was a minister of the circumcision.

questions.question: Why did the Gentiles glorify God according to Romans 15:9?
questions.explanation: Romans 15:9 indicates that the Gentiles might glorify God for his mercy.

questions.question: What should the Gentiles do with his people according to Romans 15:10?
questions.explanation: Romans 15:10 states that the Gentiles should rejoice with his people.

questions.question: According to Romans 15:11, who should praise the Lord?
questions.explanation: Romans 15:11 calls for all ye Gentiles to praise the Lord.

questions.question: Is it true that Christ pleased himself according to Romans 15:3?
questions.explanation: Romans 15:3 states that even Christ pleased not himself.

questions.question: Is it true that we should bear the infirmities of the weak according to Romans 15:1?
questions.explanation: Romans 15:1 instructs us to bear the infirmities of the weak.

questions.question: Is it true that the Gentiles are only mentioned once in Romans 15?
questions.explanation: The Gentiles are mentioned multiple times in Romans 15, specifically in verses 9, 10, and 11.

questions.question: Is it true that the God of patience and consolation is mentioned in Romans 15:5?
questions.explanation: Romans 15:5 refers to the God of patience and consolation.

medium.title: Romans Chapter 15 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Romans Chapter 15 to real-life situations.

questions.question: According to Romans 15:12, who shall rise to reign over the Gentiles?
questions.explanation: The answer is found in Romans 15:12, where it states that 'There shall be a root of Jesse, and he that shall rise to reign over the Gentiles.'

questions.question: What does Romans 15:13 promise will happen if someone abounds in hope?
options: They will be filled with joy and peace
questions.correctAnswer: They will be filled with joy and peace
questions.explanation: This is stated in Romans 15:13, which says that God will fill you with all joy and peace in believing, that you may abound in hope.

questions.question: What is Paul persuaded about the brethren in Romans 15:14?
questions.explanation: Romans 15:14 states that Paul is persuaded that they are full of goodness, filled with all knowledge, able also to admonish one another.

questions.question: What does Romans 15:15 indicate Paul has written to the brethren?
questions.explanation: Romans 15:15 says that Paul has written more boldly to them, putting them in mind because of the grace given to him by God.

questions.question: What was Paul's role regarding the Gentiles according to Romans 15:16?
options: A prophet of the Old Testament
questions.explanation: Romans 15:16 states that Paul should be the minister of Jesus Christ to the Gentiles, ministering the gospel of God.

questions.question: What does Paul mention in Romans 15:17 that he can glory in?
questions.explanation: Paul mentions in Romans 15:17 that he has whereof he may glory through Jesus Christ in those things which pertain to God.

questions.question: According to Romans 15:18, what does Paul not dare to speak of?
options: What Christ has not wrought by him
questions.correctAnswer: What Christ has not wrought by him
questions.explanation: Romans 15:18 indicates that Paul will not dare to speak of any things which Christ hath not wrought by him.

questions.question: What does Romans 15:19 say Paul has fully preached?
questions.explanation: In Romans 15:19, Paul states that he has fully preached the gospel of Christ from Jerusalem and round about unto Illyricum.

questions.question: What does Romans 15:20 say about where Paul strives to preach the gospel?
options: Where no foundation has been laid
questions.correctAnswer: Where no foundation has been laid
questions.explanation: According to Romans 15:20, Paul has strived to preach the gospel not where Christ was named, lest he should build upon another man's foundation.

questions.question: What is written in Romans 15:21 regarding those who have not heard?
questions.explanation: Romans 15:21 quotes that 'To whom he was not spoken of, they shall see: and they that have not heard shall understand.'

questions.question: According to Romans 15:22, why has Paul been hindered from coming to the brethren?
questions.explanation: Romans 15:22 states that Paul has been much hindered from coming to the brethren for which cause.

questions.question: According to Romans 15:1, what should the strong do?
options: Bear the infirmities of the weak
questions.correctAnswer: Bear the infirmities of the weak
questions.explanation: Romans 15:1 instructs that the strong ought to bear the infirmities of the weak and not please themselves.

questions.question: Is it true that Romans 15:4 emphasizes the importance of learning from past scriptures?
questions.explanation: Romans 15:4 states that whatsoever things were written aforetime were written for our learning.

questions.question: Is it false that Romans 15:5 asks for God to grant like-mindedness among believers?
questions.explanation: Romans 15:5 does indeed ask for God to grant likemindedness one toward another according to Christ Jesus.

questions.question: Is it false that Romans 15:8 states Jesus Christ was a minister of the circumcision for the truth of God?
questions.explanation: Romans 15:8 affirms that Jesus Christ was a minister of the circumcision for the truth of God, confirming the promises made unto the fathers.

hard.title: Romans Chapter 15 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Romans Chapter 15.

questions.question: In Romans 15:23, what reason does Paul give for now having no more place in these parts?
options: Having a great desire these many years to come unto you
Having completed his ministry in Jerusalem
Lack of acceptance from the local churches
Being physically weak and unable to travel
questions.correctAnswer: Having a great desire these many years to come unto you
questions.explanation: Romans 15:23 states, 'But now having no more place in these parts, and having a great desire these many years to come unto you;' indicating his desire to visit them as the reason for no more place.

questions.question: According to Romans 15:24, why does Paul trust to see the believers on his journey to Spain?
options: To be brought on my way thitherward by you
To receive financial support from them
To establish new churches in their region
To hold a public debate with local leaders
questions.correctAnswer: To be brought on my way thitherward by you
questions.explanation: Romans 15:24 says, 'for I trust to see you in my journey, and to be brought on my way thitherward by you,' showing Paul's expectation of their fellowship and support.

questions.question: What is Paul's immediate destination before going to Spain as stated in Romans 15:25?
options: Jerusalem to minister unto the saints
questions.correctAnswer: Jerusalem to minister unto the saints
questions.explanation: Romans 15:25 clearly states, 'But now I go unto Jerusalem to minister unto the saints,' indicating his immediate travel plans.

questions.question: In Romans 15:26, who made a contribution for the poor saints at Jerusalem?
questions.explanation: Romans 15:26 states, 'For it hath pleased them of Macedonia and Achaia to make a certain contribution for the poor saints which are at Jerusalem.'

questions.question: What reason does Paul give in Romans 15:27 for Macedonia and Achaia's contribution to Jerusalem?
options: Because if the Gentiles have been made partakers of their spiritual things, their duty is also to minister unto them in carnal things
To gain favor with the Jewish believers
To fulfill a legal requirement of the Law
questions.correctAnswer: Because if the Gentiles have been made partakers of their spiritual things, their duty is also to minister unto them in carnal things
questions.explanation: Romans 15:27 explains, 'For if the Gentiles have been made partakers of their spiritual things, their duty is also to minister unto them in carnal things,' showing mutual obligation.

questions.question: According to Romans 15:29, how does Paul describe his coming to the believers?
options: In the fulness of the blessing of the gospel of Christ
questions.correctAnswer: In the fulness of the blessing of the gospel of Christ
questions.explanation: Romans 15:29 states, 'I shall come in the fulness of the blessing of the gospel of Christ,' describing the spiritual abundance expected upon his arrival.

questions.question: What does the Greek word 'minister' (diakoneō) in Romans 15:25 primarily mean?
questions.explanation: In Romans 15:25, 'minister' (Greek: diakoneō) means 'to serve or attend to,' often used to describe Paul's service to the saints in Jerusalem.

questions.question: Which literary device is prominently used in Romans 15:27 where Paul speaks about spiritual and carnal things?
questions.explanation: Romans 15:27 uses parallelism by contrasting 'spiritual things' and 'carnal things' in a balanced structure to illustrate mutual obligations.

questions.question: Which Old Testament passage is echoed in Romans 15:9 where Paul mentions that the Gentiles might glorify God for his mercy?
questions.explanation: Romans 15:9 quotes Psalm 18:49, 'For this cause I will confess to thee among the Gentiles, and sing unto thy name,' connecting Gentile praise to Old Testament prophecy.

questions.question: Romans 15:12 refers to 'a root of Jesse' who will reign over the Gentiles. Which prophecy does this fulfill?
questions.explanation: Romans 15:12 alludes to Isaiah 11:1 about 'a root of Jesse' who rises to reign, fulfilling Messianic prophecy regarding Christ's reign over Gentiles.

questions.question: What comes immediately before Paul's declaration in Romans 15:23 about having no more place in these parts?
options: Paul's explanation of being hindered from coming to the Romans
Paul's description of his ministry from Jerusalem to Illyricum
Paul's greeting and thanksgiving to the Romans
Paul's teaching on bearing one another's infirmities
questions.correctAnswer: Paul's explanation of being hindered from coming to the Romans
questions.explanation: Romans 15:22 precedes verse 23 with, 'For which cause also I have been much hindered from coming to you,' explaining the delay before his desire to visit.

questions.question: In Romans 15:16, Paul speaks of the offering up of the Gentiles being acceptable. What concept does this highlight?
questions.explanation: Romans 15:16 mentions 'being sanctified by the Holy Ghost,' emphasizing the spiritual purification and acceptance of Gentile believers' offerings.

questions.question: How does Paul describe his ministry efforts in Romans 15:19?
options: Through mighty signs and wonders, by the power of the Spirit of God
questions.correctAnswer: Through mighty signs and wonders, by the power of the Spirit of God
questions.explanation: Romans 15:19 states Paul’s ministry was 'Through mighty signs and wonders, by the power of the Spirit of God,' highlighting the supernatural element of his work.

questions.question: Romans 15:4 highlights that the things written aforetime were written for what purpose?
options: Our learning, that we through patience and comfort of the scriptures might have hope
To restrict Gentile access to God
questions.correctAnswer: Our learning, that we through patience and comfort of the scriptures might have hope
questions.explanation: Romans 15:4 explains the Old Testament was written for 'our learning, that we through patience and comfort of the scriptures might have hope,' emphasizing its teaching role.

questions.question: True or False: Romans 15:30 urges believers to strive together with Paul in prayers for his deliverance from unbelievers in Judaea.
questions.explanation: Romans 15:30 says, 'Now I beseech you... that ye strive together with me in your prayers to God for me... That I may be delivered from them that do not believe in Judaea;' confirming the call to prayer.

theological.title: Romans Chapter 15 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Romans Chapter 15 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What doctrine does Romans 15:1 teach about sanctification?
options: The strong ought to bear the infirmities of the weak and not please themselves
Sanctification is a personal and isolated process
The weak are responsible for strengthening themselves
questions.correctAnswer: The strong ought to bear the infirmities of the weak and not please themselves
questions.explanation: Romans 15:1 teaches that sanctification involves mutual care within the community, where the strong bear with the weak and avoid self-pleasing, emphasizing communal holiness.

questions.question: What doctrine does Romans 15:4 teach about the role of Scripture in salvation?
options: Scriptures were written for our learning so that through patience and comfort we might have hope
Scriptures are only for historical knowledge without practical benefit
Patience is unrelated to the comfort of the Scriptures
questions.correctAnswer: Scriptures were written for our learning so that through patience and comfort we might have hope
questions.explanation: Romans 15:4 states that Scriptures were written beforehand for our instruction, so that through endurance and encouragement from the Scriptures, believers may have hope, highlighting Scripture’s role in salvation.

questions.question: What doctrine does Romans 15:16 teach about the ministry of the gospel?
options: Paul’s ministry to the Gentiles is to present them as an acceptable offering, sanctified by the Holy Spirit
The gospel ministry is limited to Jewish believers
Sanctification is unrelated to the offering of the Gentiles
The Holy Spirit does not sanctify the offering of the Gentiles
questions.correctAnswer: Paul’s ministry to the Gentiles is to present them as an acceptable offering, sanctified by the Holy Spirit
questions.explanation: Romans 15:16 explains that Paul’s role is to minister the gospel to the Gentiles so that their offering may be sanctified by the Holy Spirit and acceptable to God, showing the integration of gospel ministry and sanctification.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Romans 15:5 specifically demonstrate?
questions.explanation: Romans 15:5 calls God the God of patience (longsuffering) and consolation, indicating His enduring patience and ability to grant unity according to Christ.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Romans 15:13 specifically demonstrate?
questions.explanation: Romans 15:13 portrays God as the one who fills believers with joy and peace through believing, enabling them to abound in hope by the Holy Spirit’s power, demonstrating His sovereign work in believers’ lives.

questions.question: How does Romans 15:8–9 connect to the broader theme of God's redemptive plan in Scripture?
options: It shows Christ fulfilling promises to the patriarchs while extending mercy to the Gentiles
It limits salvation only to the circumcised
It denies God’s promises to the Jewish fathers
It emphasizes human effort over divine promise
questions.correctAnswer: It shows Christ fulfilling promises to the patriarchs while extending mercy to the Gentiles
questions.explanation: Romans 15:8–9 highlights Jesus as minister to the circumcision to confirm God’s promises to the fathers and that Gentiles might glorify God for His mercy, emphasizing fulfillment of God’s redemptive promises to both Jews and Gentiles.

questions.question: What redemptive-historical connection is emphasized by Romans 15:21?
options: The gospel is preached to those who have not heard, fulfilling prophecy
The gospel is restricted to those who already know Christ
The Old Testament is irrelevant for Gentiles
Faith is independent of hearing the gospel
questions.correctAnswer: The gospel is preached to those who have not heard, fulfilling prophecy
questions.explanation: Romans 15:21 quotes Isaiah to show that the gospel is going to those who previously had no knowledge of Christ, fulfilling the prophetic mission to bring salvation to the Gentiles.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Romans 15:14 and 15:15 teach about the role of grace and knowledge in the Christian community?
options: Believers are full of goodness and knowledge and are admonished boldly by grace
Grace eliminates the need for knowledge
Boldness in teaching comes from human effort alone
questions.correctAnswer: Believers are full of goodness and knowledge and are admonished boldly by grace
questions.explanation: Romans 15:14–15 show that believers are mature, knowledgeable, and able to admonish one another, and Paul writes boldly because of the grace given to him, linking grace and knowledge in community instruction.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Romans 15:19 and 15:20 teach about the apostolic mission and the spread of the gospel?
options: The gospel is to be preached through signs and wonders and in new regions without building on another’s foundation
The gospel is spread primarily by human wisdom
Signs and wonders are optional and unrelated to obedience
Preaching should only occur where Christ is already known
questions.correctAnswer: The gospel is to be preached through signs and wonders and in new regions without building on another’s foundation
questions.explanation: Romans 15:19–20 describe Paul’s ministry through the Spirit’s power with signs and wonders, striving to preach where Christ was not named, emphasizing pioneering mission work.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Romans 15:26 and 15:27 teach about the relationship between Jewish and Gentile believers?
options: Gentiles are indebted to help the Jewish saints because they share in spiritual blessings
Jewish believers owe nothing to Gentiles
Spiritual blessings do not require reciprocal support
The offering to Jerusalem is purely voluntary without spiritual significance
questions.correctAnswer: Gentiles are indebted to help the Jewish saints because they share in spiritual blessings
questions.explanation: Romans 15:26–27 teach that Gentile believers owe a debt of service to Jewish saints because they partake of their spiritual gifts, thus showing mutual responsibility within the body of Christ.

questions.question: Sceptics claim that Romans 15:30–31 teaches that Paul relies on human effort for deliverance. What does the passage actually teach?
options: Paul requests prayer for deliverance and service acceptance, depending on God’s intervention
Paul claims deliverance comes from his own power
Prayer is unnecessary for apostolic ministry
Paul’s deliverance is guaranteed regardless of prayer
questions.correctAnswer: Paul requests prayer for deliverance and service acceptance, depending on God’s intervention
questions.explanation: Romans 15:30–31 shows Paul exhorting believers to pray for him so that he may be delivered and his ministry accepted, affirming reliance on God’s power rather than human effort alone.

questions.question: What doctrine does Romans 15:6 teach about the purpose of unity in the church?
options: Unity leads to glorifying God with one mind and one mouth
Unity is optional and unrelated to glorifying God
Glorifying God does not require unity
Unity is primarily for human satisfaction
questions.correctAnswer: Unity leads to glorifying God with one mind and one mouth
questions.explanation: Romans 15:6 teaches that believers united in mind and speech glorify God the Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, emphasizing unity’s role in worship and glorification.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Romans 15:33 specifically demonstrate?
questions.explanation: Romans 15:33 concludes with a benediction invoking God as the God of peace, highlighting His divine attribute of peace toward His people.

questions.question: How does Romans 15:7 contribute to the theological understanding of Christ’s reception of believers?
options: Believers should receive one another as Christ also received them to God’s glory
Christ’s reception is conditional on human merit
Believers should only receive those like themselves
Reception of others is unrelated to Christ’s example
questions.correctAnswer: Believers should receive one another as Christ also received them to God’s glory
questions.explanation: Romans 15:7 instructs believers to accept each other as Christ accepted them, linking mutual reception with glorifying God and reflecting Christ’s gracious reception.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Romans 15:3 and 15:12 teach about Christ’s role in salvation history?
options: Christ did not please Himself and fulfills prophecy as the root of Jesse over the Gentiles
Christ sought His own pleasure and is unrelated to prophecy
Salvation is independent of Christ’s obedience
The root of Jesse is a separate figure from Christ
questions.correctAnswer: Christ did not please Himself and fulfills prophecy as the root of Jesse over the Gentiles
questions.explanation: Romans 15:3 emphasizes Christ’s self-denial, and 15:12 cites Isaiah’s prophecy of the root of Jesse reigning over Gentiles, together teaching Christ’s obedient fulfillment of messianic prophecy.
